instructions: Peel and core the 3 apples and cut them into 1/2 inch pieces. Roughly chop 1/4 cup of the pecans.
Pat the 1.5 lb of chops dry with paper towels and sprinkle them on both sides with 3/4 tsp of the salt and the 1/2 tsp pepper.
Put the chopped pecans in a large dry skillet over medium heat and stir them for 2 to 3 minutes, until they smell toasty and turn a shade darker. Tip them into a small bowl.

Turn the heat under the skillet to medium high and add the 1 tbsp oil and 1 tbsp of the butter. When the butter foams, lay in the chops and leave them alone for 4 minutes, until they're golden brown underneath and let go of the pan.

Flip them and cook the other side for 3 to 4 minutes. You're cooking them to 145°F in the thickest part, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest chop: it's done when the middle is faintly pink and the juices run clear. Move the chops to a plate and cover them loosely with foil.

Turn the heat to medium and add the last 1 tbsp butter to the skillet. Add the apples, the 2 tbsp brown sugar, 1/2 tsp cinnamon, the pinch of nutmeg and the remaining 1/4 tsp salt, and stir to coat the apples, scraping up the brown bits from the pan.
Pour in 1/3 cup of water, cover the skillet and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring once or twice, until the apples are soft enough to crush with a spoon.

Take off the lid and mash the apples with a fork or potato masher, leaving it a little chunky. If it's watery, let it bubble for a minute more. Pour in any juices from the chops' plate. Taste it, and add a pinch more salt if it's flat.
Spoon the applesauce over the chops and scatter the toasted pecans on top. Serve with mashed potatoes or green beans.
method_notes: All three brown the chops in a skillet and cook tart apples with sugar and cinnamon alongside. Taste of Home (the most reviewed; its page gives a review count of 77 rather than a rating count) sears boneless loin chops in butter to 145°F, then cooks sliced apples, brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg and pecans in the same pan into a syrupy topping. Mr. Food simmers sliced Granny Smiths with sugar, water, cinnamon and nutmeg into applesauce and pan fries floured shoulder chops in butter with onion; Food.com mashes a slow cooked chunky applesauce with brown sugar, vanilla and lemon and serves it on crumb coated chops. This one follows Taste of Home's pan and seasoning but adds a little water and mashes the apples into a chunky applesauce, keeping the pecans toasted on top.
